samples.summary: New dev endpoint writes bundles and screenshots into `<repoRoot>/.wb-reports/`, but `.wb-reports/` is not gitignored
samples.evidence: `report-endpoint.ts` does `mkdirSync(path.join(options.repoRoot, ".wb-reports", bundle.sessionId))` and writes `bundle.json` plus decoded PNG/JPEG bytes; `packages/frontend/vite.config.ts:200` mounts it with `repoRoot: path.resolve(__dirname, "../..")`. `.gitignore` (whole file read, 195 lines) has no `.wb-reports` entry — it lists `.harness-reports/`, `.hunt/`, `.worktrees/` but not this one. Untracked screenshot files then appear in every `git status`, and `.github/workflows/agent-implement.yml:262` explicitly instructs the agent loop to run `git add -A`, which would commit screenshots that the design itself says may contain another person's document.

samples.summary: `types: ["vite/client"]` excludes @types/node, but the new `src/plugin/**` files import node builtins and use `Buffer`
samples.evidence: The tsconfig hunk adds `"types": ["vite/client"]` while `include` stays `src/**/*`. `packages/debug-report/src/plugin/report-endpoint.ts:33-34` imports `node:fs` and `node:path`, uses `Buffer.concat`/`Buffer.from`, and `src/plugin/report-endpoint.test.ts:1-3` imports `node:fs`, `node:os`, `node:path`. Restricting `types` suppresses automatic inclusion of `@types/node`, so those ambient module declarations and the `Buffer` global are no longer in the program. This breaks `pnpm --filter @wafflebase/debug-report typecheck`, which `scripts/verify-self.mjs:344` runs as the `debug-report:check` lane (nothing in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs it — grep for `debug-report` and `typecheck` there returns no matches, so no other lane will catch it).

samples.summary: Frontend's Vite config now statically imports the plugin, which statically imports `@anthropic-ai/sdk` — a package declared only as a devDependency of debug-report
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/vite.config.ts:10` does `import { debugReportPlugin } from "@wafflebase/debug-report/plugin"`; `src/plugin/index.ts` re-exports `./draft-endpoint.ts`, which does a top-level `import Anthropic from "@anthropic-ai/sdk"`. `apply: "serve"` gates the middleware, not the import, so config evaluation for `vite build` also loads the SDK. `packages/debug-report/package.json:21` lists `@anthropic-ai/sdk` under `devDependencies`, and `packages/frontend/package.json:58` only depends on `@wafflebase/debug-report`. Any install that omits dev dependencies for the workspace (e.g. a `--prod` or narrowly filtered install, as `Dockerfile:83` does for backend) makes the frontend config fail to load. Fix belongs on the new code: make the SDK import lazy inside `draftBundle`, or move it to `dependencies`.

samples.summary: `HostAdapter.locate()` is now a dead seam — no caller anywhere, and the only host built never receives a locator
samples.evidence: `createDevHost({ route: () => routeRef.current })` at `packages/frontend/src/debug/mount.tsx:37` omits `locateOnCanvas`, so `host.locate()` (`packages/debug-report/src/ui/host.ts:157-162`) can only ever return `undefined`. A repo-wide grep for `host.locate` / `.locate(` over `packages/**/*.{ts,tsx}` finds no call site at all — locating now goes exclusively through the `locateOnCanvas` prop on `DebugOverlay` (`mount.tsx:43`). The interface member is left describing a contract nothing honours or uses.

samples.summary: Design doc and package READMEs still describe the pre-change `HostAdapter` contract and package shape
samples.evidence: `docs/design/debug-report.md:314` still declares `draft(items: readonly DebugItem[]): Promise<DraftResult>` and a single-argument `send(bundle)`, but `packages/debug-report/src/host.ts` now declares `draft(): Promise<unknown>` and `send(bundle, captures: readonly CapturePayload[])`. `packages/README.md:36` still says the package has "No React", and `packages/debug-report/README.md:19` still describes a file table from before `src/ui`, `src/plugin` and `src/testing` existed. Nothing enforces these (the backticked-path check only validates paths, and READMEs are not top-level design docs), so they will silently mislead the next implementer of a second host.
searchedFor: grep HostAdapter across docs and packages

samples.summary: Client checks for a `refused` field the report endpoint never returns on success
samples.evidence: `createDevHost.send` reads `(answer.data as {refused?: unknown}).refused` and turns a non-empty array into a send failure, but `report-endpoint.ts` returns refused captures only as a 400 (`send(res, 400, { error: \`refused ${refused.length} capture(s)...\` })`) and its 200 body is `{ ref, captures }` with no `refused` key. The client branch is unreachable, and the two halves of the new transport disagree about the success payload — a later change to either side has no test or type holding them together.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: report-endpoint.ts:63,257-265 writes decoded image bytes and bundle.json into `<repoRoot>/.wb-reports/<sessionId>/`, and vite.config.ts:200 sets repoRoot to the checkout root (`packages/frontend/../..`). No ignore rule covers it anywhere: the full root .gitignore (lines 1-195) lists `.harness-reports/`, `*.actual.png`, `*.diff.png`, `.worktrees/`, `.hunt/` etc. but not `.wb-reports`; the only other .gitignore files (packages/backend, packages/frontend, packages/sheets) contain no matching pattern; `.git/info/exclude` is the untouched git default; and no script or workflow writes ignore rules or uses --exclude-from. The endpoint also does not emit a self-ignoring `.gitignore` into the directory. The downstream consumer is real: .github/workflows/agent-implement.yml:262 instructs `git add -A`, which would stage these artifacts — the same hazard capture-collect.yml:201 and eval-score.yml:223-236 explicitly avoid. In-lane for blast radius as a repo-hygiene invariant (generated artifact dirs are ignored) that pre-existing tooling outside the diff relies on; fix belongs in .gitignore next to line 173.

This breaks `pnpm --filter @wafflebase/debug-report typecheck`, which `scripts/verify-self.mjs:344` runs as the `debug-report:check` lane (nothing in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs it — grep for `debug-report` and `typecheck` there returns no matches, so no other lane will catch it).

verdict.reason: The finding's evidence checks out as described. packages/debug-report/tsconfig.json:24-26 sets "types": ["vite/client"] while include stays "src/**/*" (lines 28-30); the config extends nothing, the package has no ambient .d.ts (glob for packages/debug-report/**/*.d.ts is empty), and there is no /// <reference types="node" /> anywhere under packages/. Meanwhile src/plugin/report-endpoint.ts:32-33 imports node:fs and node:path and uses Buffer at 80, 81, 95, 166, 201, and src/plugin/report-endpoint.test.ts:1-3 imports node:fs/node:os/node:path with Buffer.from at 9 and 73 - that test file lives under src/, so it is in the tsc program. @types/node is only a devDependency (package.json:24), and a restricted types array suppresses automatic @types inclusion, so "Cannot find module 'node:fs'" / "Cannot find name 'Buffer'" is the expected result; it would surface only in the debug-report:check lane (package.json:17 typecheck, scripts/verify-self.mjs:343-348), which has no CI-workflow duplicate. The one counter-signal is packages/design-sandbox/tsconfig.json:46, which uses the identical types: ["vite/client"] with node: imports in included sources (src/tokens/core-adapter.ts:57-59, src/scenes/aliases.ts:14) and is typechecked by scripts/verify-self.mjs:322-341 - but that is equally consistent with design-sandbox carrying the same latent breakage, and I cannot run tsc or inspect vite's shipped declarations (node_modules is not installed) to settle which. Ambiguity keeps the finding; it is in-lane for blast radius because a config restriction breaks compilation of sibling files the diff does not show.

verdict.reason: The code facts are as quoted (frontend/vite.config.ts:10 statically imports the plugin entry; plugin/index.ts:17 re-exports draft-endpoint.ts, which does a value-level top-level `import Anthropic from "@anthropic-ai/sdk"` at :25 and uses it at :171/:237; the SDK is a devDependency at debug-report/package.json:21 and absent from frontend/package.json). But the asserted breaking impact has no reachable path in this repo, which is what makes it non-blocking under the blast-radius rubric. The cited `Dockerfile:83` `--prod` install is filtered to `@wafflebase/backend...` and that image never contains or builds packages/frontend (manifests copied at Dockerfile:12-16/:73-76, sources at :25-29, builds at :34-53 — frontend appears nowhere), so the frontend vite config is never evaluated there. A repo-wide grep shows Dockerfile:22 and :83 are the ONLY filtered/prod installs, both backend-only; every path that does evaluate the frontend config uses a full install including workspace devDependencies (publish-ghpage.yml:125-126 `pnpm i` + `pnpm build:all`, ci.yml:300/:524/:654, run-browser-tests-docker.sh:119), and pnpm-lock.yaml:399-401 pins the SDK for packages/debug-report. Vite's config loader externalises bare specifiers resolved against the importer (the debug-report source), so the SDK resolves from debug-report's own tree, not frontend's. No caller or entry point is left broken or inconsistent, so the rubric's `major` bar (a broken caller / reachable bypass) is not met. The residual concern — a runtime import from a devDependency in the `./plugin` entry — is dependency/packaging hygiene owned by design-fit, and is already recorded there (.agent-review/design-fit/verdict.json:107); the package is `private: true` (debug-report/package.json:4) and is not published by npm-publish.yml (cli only), so no external consumer is affected either.
